what: A beveled glass circle (or a rounded square with a circular hole in the center) bends the background color and text behind it at refractive index 1.45, splits red, green and blue by .06 so a rainbow forms along the edge, and a fresnel .35 and reflection 1.1 light appears. It tilts by the cursor’s distance from the panel center (divided by half the screen width and height × .28), so the light spot and refraction follow, and each frame closes .08 of the remaining distance — when the cursor stops for .9s it settles back to 0.

options.shape: circle (default) or square — square is a rounded square with an 88% diameter hole in the center (corner radius 12.467%)
options.text: CSS selector for the back text to refract — searched inside the nearest section or footer. If none is found, only the background color is used
options.tilt: Cursor tilt, default .28 (original process row is .4, 0 means no tilt)
options.bevel: Bevel width — 26 for the circle (based on 400 diameter), 5.7 for the square (based on 100)

use: …
note: The panel sits stacked over the text behind it (if the text is in front of the glass, refraction is not visible). Text positions are redrawn every frame so it still fits when the panel or text moves. On touch devices it only refracts without tilting

from.where: glass.js [data-glass] (original pb-glass — concept section glass circle and square splits, process row squares, footer squares and circles)
